Its moment inertia about an axis going through its centre of mass and perpendicular to its plane is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
dm=σ⋅dA=σ 2πr dr
=2πk r3 dr
M=∫dm=2πk∫0Rr3dr
=2πkR44=πkR42

questions.q:
A 34 m long ladder weighing 10 kg leans on a frictionless wall. Its feet rest on the floor 3 m away from the wall as shown in the figure. If Ff and Fw are the reaction forces of the floor and the wall, then ratio of FwFf will be :
(Use g=10 m s-2.)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Applying force balance in vertical direction

N1=mg=100 N

Applying torque balance at the bottom contact point,

mg×32=N2×5⇒N2=Fw=30 N

Applying force balance in horizontal direction

fs=N2=30 N

Net reaction at the floor will be,

Ff=N12+fs2=1002+302=10109 N

Therefore, FwFf=3010109=3109

questions.q: A mass M hangs on a massless rod of length l which rotates at a constant angular frequency. The mass M moves with steady speed in a circular path of constant radius. Assume that the system is in steady circular motion with constant angular velocity ω. The angular momentum of M about point A is LA which lies in the positive z direction and the angular momentum of M about B is LB. The correct statement for this system is:
options: <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>L</mi><mi>A</mi></msub></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>L</mi><mi>B</mi></msub></math> are both constant in magnitude and direction
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>L</mi><mi>B</mi></msub></math> is constant in direction with varying magnitude
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>L</mi><mi>B</mi></msub></math> is constant, both in magnitude and direction
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>L</mi><mi>A</mi></msub></math> is constant, both in magnitude and direction
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
We know, L→=m(r→×v→)

Now with respect to A, we always get direction
of L→ along +ve z-axis and also constant magnitude as mvr. But with respect to B, we get constant magnitude but continuously changing direction.

questions.q: As shown in the figure, a bob of mass m is tied to a massless string whose other end portion is wound on a fly wheel (disc) of radius r and mass m. When released from rest the bob starts falling vertically. When it has covered a distance of h, the angular speed of the wheel will be:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Using work-energy theorem 

mgh=12mv2+12Iω2

mgh=12mω2r2+12mr22ω2    ( since I=mr22 and v=rω )

mgh=34mω2r2

Hence, ω=4gh3r2=1r4gh3

questions.q: A cord of negligible mass is wound around the rim of a wheel supported by spokes with negligible mass. The mass of wheel is 10 kg and radius is 10 cm and it can freely rotate without any friction. Initially the wheel is at rest. If a steady pull of 20 N is applied on the cord, the angular velocity of the wheel, after the cord is unwound by 1 m , would be :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{W}_{\mathrm{F}}=20 \times 1=20 \mathrm{~J} \\ & \therefore \quad \Delta \mathrm{KE}=20 \mathrm{~J}=\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{I} \omega^2 \\ & \mathrm{I}=\mathrm{MR}^2=10 \times 0.1^2=0.1 \mathrm{~kg} \mathrm{~m}^2 \\ & \therefore \quad 20=\frac{1}{2} \times 0.1 \times \omega^2 \\ & \Rightarrow \omega=20 \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{sec}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A heavy iron bar of weight <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>12</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi></math> is having its one end on the ground and the other on the shoulder of a man. The rod makes an angle <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>60</mn><mo>°</mo></math> with the horizontal, the normal force applied by the man on bar is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Let's consider the following diagram:

For the equilibrium of the system, the net torque, according to the above figure, on the system about point A should be zero.

With reference to the above figure, the net anti-clockwise torque about A is

τa=F2L   ...1

And, the net clockwise torque about the same point is

τc=Wcosθ×L2    ...2

Equations (1) and (2) imply that

Wcosθ×L2=F2L⇒12×10×cos60°×L2=F2 L⇒F2=120×10×cos60°2=30

Hence, the required weight can be expressed as

F2=3 kg-wt

questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
By angular momentum conservation :

mv1r1=mv2r2

v1=48×10141.6×1012=3000 m s-1

questions.q: A uniform sphere of mass <math><mn>500 </mn><mi></mi><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math> rolls without slipping on a plane horizontal surface with its centre moving at a speed of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5.00</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. Its kinetic energy is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
K.E of the sphere = Translational K.E+ Rotational K.E
=12mv21+K2R2 ,K= Radius of gyration
= 12×12×210021+25

questions.q: A solid sphere is rolling without slipping on a horizontal plane. The ratio of the linear kinetic energy of the centre of mass of the sphere and rotational kinetic energy is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{KE}_{(T)}=\frac{1}{2} m v^2 \\
& \mathrm{KE}_{(R)}=\frac{1}{2} \cdot \frac{2}{5} m R^2 \cdot \frac{v^2}{R^2}=\frac{1}{2} m v^2\left(\frac{2}{5}\right)
\end{aligned}$
So, $\frac{\mathrm{KE}_{(T)}}{\mathrm{KE}_{(R)}}=\frac{5}{2}$

questions.solution: The angular momentum is defined as the vector product of linear momentum and perpendicular distance, L→=r→×p→=r→×mv→, And direction will be upward & remain constant.

questions.q: The following bodies are made to roll up (without slipping) the same inclined plane from a horizontal plane: (i) a ring of radius <math><mi>R</mi><mo>,</mo></math> (ii) a solid cylinder of radius <math><mfrac><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">R</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac></math> and (iii) a solid sphere of radius <math><mfrac><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">R</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>.</mo></math> If, in each case, the speed of the center of mass at the bottom of the incline is same, the ratio of the maximum heights they climb is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
From conservation of mechanical energy.
12mRv2+12IRωr2=mRghR⇒V22+V22=ghR
12mdv2+12Idωd2=mdghd⇒V22+V24=ghd
12msv2+12Isωs2=msghs⇒V22+V25=ghs
∴  hR:hd:hs=1:34:710=20:15:14

Distance between OO' is,

So, according to parallel axis theorem we have,

IOIO'=M12a2+b2M12a2+b2+Ma24+b24=M12a2+b2M3a2+b2=14

ω=I1ω1+I2ω2I1+I2

=12I1ω12+12I2ω22-12I1+I2I1ω1+I2ω2I1+I22

=12I1I2I1+I2ω1-ω22

Ei-Ef=I1I2ω1-ω222I1+I2

questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{t}=\sqrt{\frac{2 \ell}{\mathrm{a}_{\mathrm{cm}}}} \\ & \mathrm{a}_{\mathrm{cm}}=\frac{\mathrm{g} \sin \theta}{1+\frac{\mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{cm}}}{\mathrm{MR}^2}} \\ & \mathrm{a}_1=\mathrm{a}_{\mathrm{cm}_1}=\frac{5 \mathrm{~g} \sin \theta}{7} \ldots . . \text { Solid } \\ & \mathrm{a}_2=\mathrm{a}_{\mathrm{cm}_2}=\frac{3 \mathrm{~g} \sin \theta}{5} \ldots . . \text { Hollow } \\ & \mathrm{a}_1 \gt \mathrm{a}_2 \\ & \mathrm{t}_1 \lt \mathrm{t}_2\end{aligned}$

Therefore, x=110.

questions.q: A body of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>m</mi></math> is projected with a speed <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>u</mi></math> making an angle of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mn>45</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">o</mi></msup></math> with the ground. The angular momentum of the body about the point of projection, at the highest point is expressed as <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mrow><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt><mi>m</mi><msup><mi>u</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><mrow><mi>X</mi><mi>g</mi></mrow></mfrac></math>. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>X</mi></math> is_______.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Consider projection as shown in above diagram.

At the topmost point, velocity of the body will be ucos45°.

Therefore, we can write the required angular momentum as 

L=muH×H=mucosθu2sin2θ2g

=mu3×142g⇒X=8

questions.q: A disc of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi></math> and radius <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>R</mi></math> is free of rotate about a horizontal axis passing through its centre and perpendicular to the plane of disc. A body of same mass as that of disc is fixed at the highest point of the disc. Now the system is released, when the body comes to the lowest position, its angular speed will be <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn><msqrt><mfrac><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">R</mi></mrow></mfrac></msqrt><mo> </mo><mi>rad</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo></math> _____ .
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Let the angular speed of disc be ω.

Using conservation of mechanical energy

mg2R=12Idisc ω2+12Iparticle ω2

Where, I is moment of inertia.

⇒mg2R=ω22m22+mR2

⇒mg2R=ω2232mR2

⇒34ω2=2gR             

 ⇒ω2=8g3R

Thus, angular speed is ω=803R rad s-1

Given ω=4x3R

Comparing both, 16x3R=803R

Therefore, the value of x=5.

questions.q: A circular ring and a solid sphere having same radius roll down on an inclined plane from rest without slipping. The ratio of their velocities when reached at the bottom of the plane is $\sqrt{\frac{x}{5}}$ where $\mathrm{x}=$ _____
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Applying Mechanical Energy conservation :
$\mathrm{k}_{\mathrm{i}}+\mathrm{U}_{\mathrm{i}}=\mathrm{k}_{\mathrm{f}}+\mathrm{U}_{\mathrm{f}}$
$\begin{aligned}
& \Rightarrow 0+\mathrm{Mgh}=\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{mv}^2\left(1+\frac{\mathrm{k}^2}{\mathrm{R}^2}\right)+0 \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{~V}=\sqrt{\frac{2 \mathrm{gh}}{1+\frac{\mathrm{k}^2}{\mathrm{R}^2}}}
\end{aligned}$
So Ratio of velocities
$\frac{\mathrm{V}_{\text {Ring }}}{\mathrm{V}_{\text {solids sphere }}}=\sqrt{\frac{1+\frac{2}{5}}{1+1}}=\sqrt{\frac{7}{10}}$
$\mathrm{x}=3.5$ Rounding off $\mathrm{x}=4$
